query: My Node service uses the OpenTelemetry SDK and I want to send traces and metrics straight to Grafana Cloud with environment variables. I set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to the OTLP URL from the portal and I get 404 on traces. Also my dashboards can't find http.route as a label on my request metrics. What do I change and how do I query it?
expected_behavior: States that a signal-specific variable such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT is used as-is and must include the full path, for example https://otlp-gateway-<REGION>.grafana.net/otlp/v1/traces, whereas the base OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT gets /v1/traces appended by the SDK
Says traces must go to the OTLP gateway and not to the Tempo query URL https://<STACK>.grafana.net/tempo, which rejects them
Uses basic auth with the numeric instance ID as user and a Cloud access policy token with the traces:write scope as password

Says to copy the exact endpoint from the stack's OpenTelemetry tile or the portal rather than building it from a template, because hostname format depends on region creation date (flat before 2026-01-15, nested after)
Explains that dots in metric attribute names become underscores, so http.route is queried as http_route

Explains that resource attributes land in target_info and are joined on job and instance, for example with on(job, instance) group_left(...) target_info, and that only a default list (service.*, k8s.cluster.name, deployment.environment and similar) is promoted to labels on every series
Mentions that a collector such as Grafana Alloy is the production default and direct SDK export suits dev or test

query: I need a CPU alert in Grafana Cloud managed with Terraform, routed to the backend team's Slack. Our service sometimes stops reporting metrics for a while. Someone said we got weird alerts that ignored our mute timing during a maintenance window. How should I build the rule, the routing, and the provisioning?
expected_behavior: Uses a Grafana-managed alert rule (grafana_rule_group) with a Reduce and Threshold expression pair, where expressions use datasource_uid = "__expr__"

Explains that by default No Data and Error states raise separate DatasourceNoData and DatasourceError alerts, with labels alertname, datasource_uid and rulename, that are independent of the original alert so its silences, mute timings and policies may not apply
Suggests routing those alerts with a policy matching alertname=DatasourceError (and DatasourceNoData) grouped by datasource_uid, or choosing an explicit No Data or Error handling state on the rule
States that only labels route alerts: a team value placed in an annotation falls to the default policy, so team=backend must be a label
Notes that sibling policies stop at the first match unless Continue matching siblings is enabled, and that mute timings attach to child policies only and are not inherited
Warns that provisioning the notification policy tree (grafana_notification_policy) overwrites all existing policies because it is one resource
Says Grafana Cloud has no file provisioning, so Terraform or the HTTP API is used, with a service account token (not an access policy token) for the Alerting provisioning API
Advises avoiding query values in labels (use annotations) because a changing label value creates a different alert instance

query: I want to monitor our public API from Grafana Cloud Synthetic Monitoring: first POST to /login to get a token, then GET /orders with that token, from 4 locations every minute. Set it up and alert me when it breaks. Ours is a staging API that allows one session per user.
expected_behavior: Chooses a MultiHTTP check because a token from sign-in is needed in a second request, rather than a plain HTTP check
Warns that MultiHTTP does not validate a 200 status automatically, so assertions must be defined for each request or failures never affect uptime

Warns that every selected probe runs the check at every interval at nearly the same time, so 4 probes at 1 minute means 4 hits per minute and the single-session-per-user API must tolerate concurrent sessions
Uses per-check alerts (failed checks, and optionally latency) rather than legacy data source-managed alerts
States that Synthetic Monitoring alerts carry the label namespace = synthetic_monitoring so a child notification policy can route on it, and suggests grouping by instance and job
Mentions that private probe firewalls must allow jslib.k6.io if variables or libraries are used, or that variables are referenced as ${name}
If a Terraform resource is given, uses grafana_synthetic_monitoring_check with a multihttp block inside settings

query: Our CI scripts still create dashboards with an old Grafana API key via POST /api/dashboards/db, and our Terraform uses grafana_api_key. We use Grafana Cloud and want to migrate. I tried my Cloud access policy token against the stack's dashboard endpoint and got unauthorized. What is the right way to do this now?
expected_behavior: Explains that access policy tokens authorize telemetry and the Cloud API at grafana.com but not the instance HTTP API, so dashboards need a service account token
Replaces instance API keys and grafana_api_key with service accounts, using grafana_service_account and grafana_service_account_token in Terraform
Sends the service account token in the Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN> header
Recommends setting an expiry on the token because service account tokens have no expiry by default
Recommends moving off legacy /api routes (deprecated in Grafana 13) to /apis/<group>/<version>/namespaces/<ns>/..., using namespace stacks-<STACK_ID> on Cloud and the GA v1 version
States that the dashboard API addresses a dashboard by metadata.name (the uid) in the path, not the metadata.uid field
